translations.answer: The original thread confirms that the cycle is changed to steady_clock for the wall clock at 100 Hz, and the original author used it in multiple controllers; however, he explicitly states that this will not scale with the simulation real-time factor, so it is not a universal solution. Project members prefer that the Gazebo-like simulators use dedicated plugins/nodes to drive controller updates during physical updates, rather than the general ros2_control_node guessing the semantics of /clock. The current priority is to clarify whether the clock rate is wall clock or simulation time rate, and then select the corresponding integration; the thread does not provide a merged universal fix.
translations.applicability: Applies to simulators that publish /clock, and environments using general ros2_control_node and use_sim_time=true, such as Humble/Rolling; real hardware should not use this clock combination.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original author switched to std::chrono::steady_clock and reported that joint_trajectory_controller, forward_command_controller, and custom controllers work normally under the wall clock.
translations.details.attempts.1: Another user suggested that simulation time should start from system time and publish /clock before starting ros2_control_node, but the original author explicitly states that this depends on the startup order.
translations.details.attempts.2: A user reported in 2024 that rclcpp::Rate is effective with use_sim_time, but the code is clearly a ChatGPT-generated version and the original test code is no longer in hand.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Simulated update rate, /joint_states wall clock frequency, /clock publishing behavior, and simulation real-time factor are all recorded; do not only look at the hz value of a single topic.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Determine the semantics: the controller rate is fixed under the wall clock, or it should be updated with each simulation time and physics step.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Check if the simulator already has a dedicated plugin/nodes, such as gazebo_ros2_control, that calls controller update during physical updates.
translations.details.environments.0: Original reproduction: Ubuntu 22.04, ROS 2 Humble, simulator publishes /clock, update_rate=100 Hz, use_sim_time=true.
translations.details.environments.1: Another user reported the same issue in Humble and ros-rolling-ros2-control in 2023-10.
translations.details.limits.0: steady_clock only solves the wall clock cycle; the original author explicitly states it will not scale with the simulation real-time factor.
translations.details.limits.1: The suggestion to align simulation time with system time depends on the startup order; the responder also believes this is not universally applicable.
translations.details.limits.2: The reply from rclcpp::Rate is only from one user experience, and the code is not the original test code from that time, so it cannot be upgraded to a universal solution.
translations.details.limits.3: Real hardware should not use use_sim_time; project members point out that the time can always be zero when the simulator stops.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The main design direction proposed by the project members is to use dedicated simulator_ros2_control plugins/nodes that advance the controller with physical time, such as the Gazebo plugin.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Issue #859 was closed in 2024-11, but the thread does not link to a merged, universal fix for ros2_control_node+use_sim_time.
translations.details.outcomes.2: The PR #802 is marked as related but only addresses the catch-up behavior and is not merged, so it cannot be used as evidence for #859 being fixed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why is the actual update rate much higher than the configured update_rate when use_sim_time is set to true, and should the wall clock or simulation time be used for rate control?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: The WBC system must explicitly define the time base used in the control cycle; do not use simulation time in real hardware, and do not mistakenly treat wall clock 100 Hz as simulation time 100 Hz when the real-time factor is not verified.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The original thread confirms that ros2_control_node's cycle clock and use_sim_time combination leads to incorrect update rates, but the thread does not provide a universal single-clock solution applicable to all simulators.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Project members point out that different simulators may use /clock or other APIs, making it difficult to maintain universal semantics in the general ros2_control_node.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The original author measured about 2.5 kHz via ros2 topic hz /joint_states, but the configured value is 100 Hz.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Using steady_clock fixes the wall clock rate to 100 Hz, but when the real-time factor is 0.5, this is equivalent to a relative simulation time of 200 Hz.

translations.source.title: ros2_control uses simulation time and the update rate becomes abnormally high
translations.title: Why does 100 Hz run to thousands of Hz when use_sim_time is set to true in ros2_control_node, and how to choose the clock and update mechanism?
